title: lifedraft input contract — universal (target shape, Track C / #602)
$comment: A dated balance sheet of entities. Facts (people/accounts/liabilities/properties/estate/cash_flows), beliefs (assumptions) and questions (decisions/sensitivity) are separate top-level namespaces. additionalProperties:false everywhere: an unknown key is a load error, not a silent drop. null means 'unknown'; a field is omitted only when structurally inapplicable to a given `kind` (enforced by allOf/if/then); 0 means exactly zero (DP#32). This file holds the JURISDICTION-AGNOSTIC shape only. countries/canada/input_schema.json (this repo's overlay, at schema/countries/canada/input_schema.json) supplies Canada-specific enums (account kinds, provinces, CPP/OAS, LIRA/LSIF/RESP/FHSA sub-shapes) and is COMPOSED with this file by input_contract.compose_schema() before validation -- see that module for the merge rule. This split is a deliberate, explicit user decision (see PR body): Atlas's original draft collapsed both files into one; the two-file split is kept because ~60 open jurisdiction issues and 3 in-flight country PRs (UK/Australia/WOTC) depend on the universal/overlay seam existing.

as_of.description: The date this snapshot of the balance sheet is true. The document's root date; balances/values may carry their own, more specific as_of (DP#1).

currency.description: ISO 4217. Only CAD supported today; enum, not free string, so a typo is a load error rather than a silently-wrong unit.

dollars.description: Whether every dollar figure in this document (facts AND assumptions) is nominal (as-stated) or real (constant purchasing power, base year below). A run cannot mix the two.

real_base_year.description: Required and meaningful only when dollars=real: the year whose price level all real figures are expressed in.

country.description: Study-level default. Package presence (DP#16) still drives which jurisdiction modules load; this field is the config-side declaration that must agree with it. The Canada overlay restricts this to the const 'canada'.

province.description: $defs/province is deliberately open (non-empty string) here; the Canada overlay replaces it with the closed 13-province/territory enum.

people.description: One entity per person, any generation. Generation, household membership and 'who is the study asking about' are all DERIVED from relationships + as_of, never declared by array position (#598).

accounts.description: Every registered/non-registered account, each owned by exactly one (or jointly by named) person(s) (#599). Replaces the household-singleton portfolio.accounts.* map.

liabilities.description: Every debt: mortgages, HELOCs, revolving lines of credit, term loans. balance and limit are always separate fields (#577/#601). Revolving kinds (heloc, line_of_credit) carry a `limit`; `collateral` (nullable) is what actually distinguishes secured from unsecured -- a HELOC is a line_of_credit with `collateral` set, not a different axis (#689).

properties.description: Every parcel of real property the family owns, replacing the property/house_comparison/rental_properties three-way split (#601).

cash_flows.description: Known/planned irregular income and expenses, dated. A FACT (already decided/known), not a belief.

household_budget.description: Issue #679: a FACT about ongoing cash flow -- what the household's own budget says it actually spends per year to live. Unlike assumptions.savings_rate (a stated intention/belief), this is measured from the household's own bank/credit statements. Optional and deliberately NOT in this schema's top-level `required` list (DP#16: auto-include on trigger data) -- a document that omits it simply cannot express the cash-flow solvency constraint (simulation_rules.apply_solvency), exactly as a document without house_value/mortgage_balance/margin_available cannot express the LTV explorer. Present-and-set is what engages the check; the check is never silently skipped once the data is there. The emergency RESERVE is a separate concept and lives under assumptions.emergency_reserve (#688): it is a policy (how many months to hold, and where), not a measured spend.

installments.description: Issue #759: fixed-term, zero-interest installment OBLIGATIONS -- a medical/dental/education payment plan structured as an up-front lump (already paid, not modelled here) followed by N equal monthly payments and an optional final balloon, at 0% interest, over a FIXED term. Neither a mortgage, nor revolving credit, nor a recurring living cost: it is non-negotiable under an income shock (it does NOT compress like discretionary spending -- contrast #761's discretionary split) AND it ENDS on its declared final payment date (it is not carried to the horizon the way household_budget.annual_living_costs is). Optional and deliberately NOT in this schema's top-level `required` list (DP#16: auto-include on trigger data) -- a document that omits it has no such plan, and the run is unchanged (the golden invariant must not move, DP#32). Each plan's payments fold into the solvency identity's debt-service term and the #758 reserve/runway sizing via simulation_rules.apply_installments, and STOP the year after the final payment.

equity_grants.description: Issue #768: private-company stock options / equity grants the household HOLDS but cannot count toward solvency or runway. A private, unvested, or strike-undetermined option grant is NOT a liquid asset -- it cannot be sold, cannot pay a mortgage, and realises only on a speculative, dated liquidity event that is outside the projection. The engine values every declared grant at $0 for ALL solvency / runway / decumulation metrics (#758, #679) and surfaces it as 'recorded, valued $0' so the household knows it was not silently dropped (DP#32: an absence-of-record is not a labelled $0). Optional and deliberately NOT in this schema's top-level `required` list (DP#16: auto-include on trigger data) -- a document that omits it has no such grants, and the run is unchanged (the golden invariant must not move). The block is RECORD-ONLY: it never feeds a simulation rule (no rule reads it), so its $0 contribution is by construction, and the output names each grant explicitly rather than inventing a value for it.

estate.description: Estate FACTS: elections currently in force and insurance in force. Mortality is a BELIEF and lives under assumptions.mortality (see migration-plan.md, hard decision #1).

assumptions.description: BELIEFS: what we assume about the world (returns, inflation, mortality, rate paths, tax-law overrides). Never a fact about the balance sheet.

decisions.description: QUESTIONS: what we are deciding between. The optimizer/scenario engine compares these candidates head-to-head. Absence of a candidate list means auto-discovery from trigger data (DP#16) is still permitted, but the schema always accepts an explicit list.

private_loans.description: Issue #832: private loans from an individual. The lender is either a declared household member or an individual outside the household (inline identity). Repayment/interest terms default to on_demand/on_demand -- a demand loan with no interest demanded is modeled as interest-free financing (no tax flow). When interest IS paid/payable, the lender accrues taxable income (in their bracket, if a household member) and the borrower's interest is deductible under ITA s.20(1)(c) when use=investment; a minor lender's interest is attributed to the borrower (s.74.2). Absent/empty = no private loans (the golden household). Supersedes #813.

gifts.description: Epic #841 bite 3: parent->child cash gifts that FUND a child's registered contributions (TFSA/FHSA/RRSP) beyond what the child's own small income can. A gift REDIRECTS after-tax savings from the household adult base to a child's OWN registered accounts (DP#18: money conserved -- the adult base drops by exactly what funds the child, no double-count). TAX FACTS modeled: an inter-vivos cash gift is NOT income to the child and NOT deductible to the donor (tax-free to both). The gift is applied EACH projection year and SELF-LIMITS: once the child's registered room is filled it funds nothing further (never spilling into non-registered -- that is asset location, bite 3 scope 3). Because registered room requires age 18+ AND registered growth is tax-sheltered, ITA s.74.1 minor-attribution has NO effect on a registered-room gift (no minor can hold the room, and there is no taxable income to attribute); it would matter only for a future non-registered gift to a minor. Absent/empty = no gifts (the golden household).

first_home_purchases.description: Issue #704: a household member (today: a CHILD) becomes a FIRST-TIME HOME BUYER in a given year, using the two instruments Canada provides for a first home. In that year the member's own FHSA is withdrawn TAX-FREE (qualifying withdrawal, the account closes) and up to $60,000 comes out of their own RRSP NON-TAXABLY under the Home Buyers' Plan (HBP), repaid over a 15-year schedule (countries/canada/fhsa.py, hbp_rules.py). Both proceeds fund the down payment (net worth conserved -- the FHSA drains tax-free, the HBP is a loan owed back to the member's own RRSP). Absent/empty = no first-home purchase (the golden household).

sensitivity.description: QUESTIONS (uncertainty dimension): named overlay presets and sweep ranges layered ACROSS every decision comparison, not decisions themselves (DP#5).

provenance.description: OPTIONAL sidecar (#660, epic #659 Track 1): every key is an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into THIS document (e.g. "/accounts/0/balance/amount"), every value describes how that leaf is known. A leaf with NO entry here is `assumed` BY DEFINITION -- provenance.py's Provenance.confidence() returns "assumed" for any pointer absent from this object, so coverage is deliberately allowed to be incomplete; an author cannot dodge scrutiny by simply omitting an entry. Cross-document checks this schema fragment cannot express on its own (a pointer must resolve against the document; a plausible_range/domain must bracket/contain the leaf's actual current value) are enforced by provenance.load_provenance(), not by jsonschema.

date.description: RFC 3339 full-date (YYYY-MM-DD). Precision to the day, so month-granularity rules (CPP/OAS onset) and day-granularity rules (FHSA 15-year window, RRIF-at-71) are exact, not approximated to a year (#597).

person_id.description: Stable identifier, referenced by accounts/liabilities/properties/estate/decisions. Never role text ('primary'/'spouse') — a role is a label, not an identity (#598).

income_kind.description: Issue #674: shared by both `income` and `income_override` so a job-loss scenario and a currently-in-pay income declare the same vocabulary, never two spellings of the same fact (DP#9). Deliberately excludes 'pension' and 'government_benefit' — CPP, OAS and employer-pension facts belong ONLY in the structured `person.benefits` object, never duplicated here as a second, less precise income line (#595). 'ei' (Employment Insurance) is included here, not in `person.benefits`, because unlike CPP/OAS it is not an elected, ongoing claim — it is exactly the kind of temporary, dated income a job-loss `income_override` exists to express. `kind` is not decoration: it decides whether an amount is 'earned income' for RRSP room accrual (ITA s.146(1) excludes EI benefits — see EARNED_INCOME_KINDS in simulation.py), how it is taxed, and whether CPP/QPP contributions apply.

province.description: Jurisdiction-agnostic placeholder — a non-empty string. The Canada overlay replaces this $def wholesale with the closed enum of provinces/territories (long form only; #595 flagged 'qc' vs 'quebec' as a self-inconsistent example in the old schema).

owner_ref.description: A single person, or a jointly-held asset/liability split by percentage. Reused by account/liability/property owner fields.

money.description: A non-negative dollar amount in the document's declared currency/dollars units. Debts are recorded as positive magnitudes on liabilities, never as negative assets.

signed_money.description: A dollar amount that may legitimately be negative (e.g. a cash-flow outflow).

rate.description: An annual rate as a fraction (0.07, not 7). Negative allowed for stress scenarios (crash years, deflation).

as_of.description: Statements arrive on different dates; this need not equal the document's root as_of (#597).

type.description: Minimal generative set: 'child_of'/generation/household membership are all DERIVED by traversing these edges from any person, at the as_of date — never separately declared. Declare each relationship ONCE (e.g. only the parent declares parent_of the child); a loader-level check (#582) rejects a graph where both directions are declared inconsistently or a cycle exists.

from.description: Marriage date for spouse_of; null = unknown.

to.description: Divorce/dissolution date for spouse_of; null = ongoing or unknown. Not used for parent_of.

tuition.description: Issue #764: the ELIGIBLE tuition the person PAID for this study period, per calendar year it is in session (the same amount is paid in each year the window covers). null/absent = no tuition declared (the engine applies no tuition credit). The federal 15% non-refundable tuition credit (ITA s.118.5) is modelled on this leaf; the Quebec provincial portion (#783), carry-forward of unused amounts (#784), and transfer to a supporting spouse/parent (#785, federal $5,000 limit) are modelled. See engine issues #764/#783/#784/#785.

transfer_to.description: Issue #785: the person (spouse/parent) to whom the student TRANSFERS their unused federal tuition credit (ITA s.118.8, $5,000 annual limit). null/absent = no transfer declared; the student uses the credit against their own tax first, then carries forward the remainder (#784). For a CHILD student (#701), the child has no own tax, so the entire credit (up to $5,000) transfers to this person, reducing THEIR federal tax.

amount.description: Annual gross amount in effect over [from, to).

x-uncertainty.resolved_by: Your latest pay stub, T4, or notice of assessment.
x-uncertainty.question: What is this person's actual annual gross income?

expenses_annual.description: Issue #980 (T2125): for kind=self_employment, the total annual PROFESSIONAL EXPENSES deductible against gross fees to derive NET business income (home-office business-use-%, professional dues + mandatory liability insurance, professional development, meals/entertainment at 50% inclusion, other). The engine taxes, charges the self-employed contribution stack (#978 QPP both halves + QPIP + individual HSF), and accrues RRSP room (ITA s.146(1)) on (amount - expenses_annual), NOT on gross. Enter the expenses the SAME way the T2125 does: meals/entertainment already at the 50% inclusion amount the CRA admits, since the engine models the net total, not per-category inclusion (DP#2 -- the per-category breakdown is your record-keeping, not engine logic; DP#7 -- model the mechanism, the net-income deduction, not the branded T2125 form's line items). A single scalar matches the established convention for the structurally identical rental case ($defs/property[kind=rental].expenses_annual, CRA T776 -- one spelling of the 'net = gross - expenses' fact, DP#9, not two). Absent/null ONLY for a self-employment income with NO deductible expenses; the engine then taxes the full `amount` (byte-identical to pre-#980, DP#32 absence-safe -- a missing block is not silently zeroed expenses, it is 'no expenses declared'). Has NO effect for any other kind (employment/rental/investment/ei/other) -- the engine reads it only on a self_employment segment.

employer_rrsp_match.description: The single surviving spelling of an employer's matched-retirement-account contribution (#595E collapsed employer_benefits.members[].rrsp_match_pct, family.members[].employer_rrsp_match_pct, and employer_match_pct into this one path, attached to the income it is a term of). Jurisdiction-agnostic: 'into_account' just needs to resolve to an account id, whatever kind that account is in the active jurisdiction.

employment.description: Issue #767: employment-contract terms that constrain re-employment AFTER this income ends (a job-loss recovery income_override cannot start before the contract/law allows). Present only when kind=employment; null/absent means no contract terms are declared (modelled, not guessed — DP#32). A non_compete with a scope but no months is a PARTIAL declaration and is rejected at load (the schema requires all three of months/scope/geography when non_compete is present), never silently defaulted.

months.description: Duration of the non-competition covenant in months. Bars re-employment in the person's own specialty (the `scope`) for this window after the employment ends. A recovery income_override for this income whose `from` is earlier than termination_date + months is clamped forward to that date (issue #767), so runway is not overstated. 0 = no non-compete (explicit, not absent).

scope.description: The employer's line of business the covenant covers. Free text. Required alongside months — a non-compete with a duration but no scope is a partial declaration DP#32 forbids (it would silently narrow or widen what re-employment is barred).

geography.description: The geographic area the covenant covers. Free text. Required alongside months for the same reason as scope.

anyOf.description: A non-competition covenant. All three fields are required when the block is present: a partial declaration (e.g. months with no scope) must FAIL LOUDLY, never default the missing piece (DP#32, issue #767 acceptance).

non_compete.description: null = no non-competition covenant (explicit). Present = the covenant's terms, all three required.

probation_end.description: The date the probationary period ends. A 'now' income shock inside probation is the highest-probability termination case (flagged, not enforced). null = not on probation / past probation / unknown.

notice_days.description: Contractual pay-in-lieu-of-notice entitlement in days. Modelled as employment income continuing for this many days past the termination date (extends runway), with kind=employment so RRSP-room accrual is unchanged. 0 = no contractual notice entitlement (explicit, not absent).

employment_contract.description: Issue #767: the employment-contract terms that bound when and how income can recover after a job loss. Attached to the employment income (not the person) because the constraint travels with the income_id an income_override targets — the recovery segment for THIS income cannot precede the non-compete window.

benefit_claim.description: An already-elected or already-in-pay employer/government retirement benefit. A person who has NOT yet started a benefit omits the corresponding key entirely (not null, not zero) — candidate start ages to sweep belong in decisions.retirement_age, not here. The Canada overlay adds 'cpp' and 'oas' properties to this object (CPP/OAS are Canada-specific programs); this file only defines the jurisdiction-agnostic 'employer_pension'.

benefit_entitlement.description: Issue #650: a person's FUTURE, pre-claim government/employer retirement entitlement — the number off a statement they have NOT started drawing yet (e.g. a Service Canada CPP Statement of Contributions projecting a monthly amount at 65). Distinct from `benefit_claim`, which is a benefit ALREADY IN PAY (a committed start_date + amount). An entitlement is a dated BELIEF, not a fact: it carries the estimate and the date it was produced (estimates age), and it lets the retirement-income model begin the benefit at a MODELED claim age instead of a hardcoded start_date — which is exactly what makes the CPP/OAS claiming-age question (#291) expressible. A person who is already in pay uses `benefits`; a person with neither omits both. The Canada overlay adds 'cpp' and 'oas' properties (CPP/OAS are Canada-specific programs); this file only defines the empty jurisdiction-agnostic shell.

label.description: Human-friendly, non-PII display identifier (e.g. 'primary', 'spouse', 'child_a', 'grandparent_paternal'). DP#4-style role text as a HINT, never as the join key — id is the join key.

legal_name.description: Optional real name for the user's own copy of the document. null in any fixture/example (DP#15: no personal data in the repo).

birth_date.description: null = unknown (e.g. a deceased ancestor whose exact DOB was never recorded). Replaces birth_year everywhere (#597); every age-gated rule (RRIF@71, CPP/OAS by month, FHSA 15y window) computes from this, never from a stored age.

room.description: $defs/person_room is supplied entirely by the Canada overlay (its keys are Canada account-kind names: rrsp/tfsa/fhsa/resp). A jurisdiction with different registered-account vocabulary supplies its own person_room shape.

death_date.description: A FACT: non-null only if this person has already died as of the document's as_of. null does not mean 'assumed immortal' — projected mortality for living people is a BELIEF, see assumptions.mortality.

residency.description: Per-person, because a 4-generation family can span provinces (e.g. a grandparent who retired to another province). The document-level jurisdiction.province is the study default, not an assumption that every person shares it.

product.description: Key into assumptions.products (a synthetic/product composition registry), or a bucket name understood by the engine.

locked_until.description: Issue #823: the unlock condition for an illiquid account balance. Exactly one of `age` or `date` is declared (enforced by minProperties/maxProperties below at the overlay level; this universal def accepts either). `age` is the owner's age at which the balance becomes liquid (e.g. 65 for Fonds FTQ shares); `date` is a calendar date (ISO YYYY-MM-DD). The balance is excluded from the solvency/runway liquidation waterfall until the condition is met, and is liquid thereafter.

age.description: The owner's age at which the balance becomes liquid (DP#1: age is date-computed from the owner's birth_year, never a hardcoded constant).

date.description: A calendar date (ISO YYYY-MM-DD) at which the balance becomes liquid.

product.description: Issue #826: jurisdiction-agnostic placeholder -- a non-empty product id or null. The Canada overlay replaces this $def with the closed product enum (fonds_ftq, ...). See the account.product field description for the product-module resolution rule (DP#7/#10/#12: a product flag triggers a program module that supplies the product's well-known rules; an explicit account.expected_return / account.locked_until overrides the product default, DP#13).

owner.description: A single person for registered/individual account kinds (legally required); joint ownership only ever valid for the jurisdiction's non-registered/RESP-style kinds — enforced by the overlay's allOf.

kind.description: $defs/account_kind is a jurisdiction-agnostic placeholder (non-empty string) here. The Canada overlay replaces that $def with the closed account-kind enum (rrsp/tfsa/fhsa/resp/lira/... ) and adds the corresponding kind-specific sub-objects (fhsa/lira/lsif/resp) and allOf conditionals to THIS ($defs/account) object.

acb.description: Adjusted cost base. null = unknown (must be estimated/obtained, not assumed equal to balance). Meaningful mainly for non-registered/taxable-on-disposition kinds; other kinds carry null.

beneficiary.description: Who receives the account's VALUE at death (registered plans lose the shelter unless successor_holder applies instead) (#600).

successor_holder.description: A spouse who inherits the account itself and keeps it tax-sheltered forever — materially different from `beneficiary` (#600). Which account kinds this is legal for is jurisdiction-specific (in Canada: TFSA only); the overlay's allOf enforces null elsewhere.

contributors.description: Only meaningful for a spousal-contribution registered account: the annuitant/owner is `owner`; this lists who actually contributes (attribution rules need both). Jurisdiction-specific whether this concept exists at all.

product.description: Issue #826 (DP#7/#10/#12): a branded-product flag that triggers a program module encoding the product's well-known, identical-for-every-holder rules -- so the household does NOT restate them in input. e.g. 'fonds_ftq' resolves to countries/canada/fonds_ftq.py: a 7.3% 10-year-CAR expected return and locked-until-age-65 illiquidity (plus the LSIF credit already modeled in lsif_credit.py). null = a generic account with no product-module rules (the default; today's behaviour). The product supplies expected_return/locked_until DEFAULTS into the same #823 downstream machinery; an explicit account.expected_return / account.locked_until on the same account OVERRIDES the product default (DP#13: a declared value wins over a fallback). $defs/product is a jurisdiction-agnostic placeholder (non-empty string or null) here; the Canada overlay replaces that $def with the closed product enum (fonds_ftq, ...).

expected_return.description: Issue #823/#826: per-account expected-return override (a real annual rate, e.g. 0.073 for Fonds FTQ's 10-year CAR). null = use the global return_model rate, OR -- when the account declares a `product` whose module supplies a product default (issue #826, e.g. fonds_ftq -> 7.3%) -- use that product default (the default; preserves today's behaviour when no product is declared). When declared, the engine blends this account's balance into its account-kind pot at this rate (balance-weighted with the rest of the pot at the global rate), so a flagged account grows at its own rate while unflagged accounts use the global rate. DP#13: an explicit expected_return here wins over a product-module default. Numerically small for FTQ (7.3% vs 7% global) but makes the holding's own return profile explicit and non-silently-substituted (DP#32).

mer.description: Issue #691: this account's all-in management-expense-ratio (a real annual fraction, e.g. 0.0116 for a 1.16% fund). Subtracted from the account's GROSS growth rate before compounding, so a declared fee actually reduces the balance (net = gross - mer). The gross rate is the global `return_model` rate, or this account's #823 `expected_return`/product blend when declared -- MER composes on top (net = expected_return - mer). Applied balance-weighted into the account-kind pot the growth rule reads (rrsp/tfsa/fhsa/non_reg/lira/lif), the same seam #823's expected_return rides. 0.0 means fee-free (a declared fact -- reaches the config, distinct from null), NOT 'unknown'; null = no MER declared, the global fee-free rate (today's behaviour; keeps the golden invariant unchanged). This is the ONE canonical fee spelling the engine reads (DP#8): the per-fund `assumptions.products.*.mer` catalog datum is a future per-holding source that aggregates into this account-level fee; the duplicate `asset_location.PortfolioHolding.mer_pct` was deleted.
mer.$comment: #691: the engine-consumed MER. Canonical over the two former dead fee fields (DP#8).

locked_until.description: Issue #823/#826: per-account illiquidity. The balance is NOT liquid (excluded from the solvency/runway liquidation waterfall) before the unlock condition is met; it IS liquid after. null = fully liquid, OR -- when the account declares a `product` whose module supplies a product default (issue #826, e.g. fonds_ftq -> locked-until-65) -- use that product default. Modeled on the #768 equity-grant illiquidity concept, but FTQ shares become accessible at age 65 / a qualifying event, so this is 'illiquid-until-65', not 'zero forever'. DP#13: an explicit locked_until here wins over a product-module default. The retirement drawdown rule may draw the balance after the unlock (a read of this flag); before the unlock the runway/solvency waterfall cannot liquidate it.

liability_kind.description: 'heloc' and 'line_of_credit' are the SAME mechanism (revolving, interest-only, has a `limit`) at two points on the `collateral` axis -- a HELOC is a line_of_credit secured by a property (#664/#681's charge applies to it); `line_of_credit` with `collateral: null` is the unsecured case a real signed facility can be (#689). They stay two enum values rather than collapsing to one because `heloc` alone carries the mortgage-paired readvance mechanic (`readvanceable`/`capitalize_interest`, below) that only makes sense wired to a specific mortgaged property; a `line_of_credit` never has those two fields, secured or not.

deductibility.description: Traced fractions (e.g. ITA §20(1)(c) in Canada), not derived — the schema records the tracing state directly rather than reconstructing it from a single blended rate (#601).

amount.description: The cash-back the lender pays the household AT ORIGINATION (a positive inflow to the household). Small relative to the tranche (e.g. $1,200 for a $600k+ house tranche). The adapter credits it as an origination_cash_back cash-flow in the projection's first year.

clawback_rate.description: The FRACTION of the cash-back repaid to the lender if the mortgage is FULLY prepaid before term_years elapse (e.g. 0.5 = half). A contingent charge, not an accrual: it is owed only on an early full prepayment, and the engine does not model that event for a year-0 mortgage yet (#1075 optimizer half).

term_years.description: The cash-back's retention term: if the mortgage is fully prepaid within this many years of origination, clawback_rate of the amount is owed back to the lender; after it, the cash-back is fully vested.

min_house_amount.description: Issue #1075 (optimizer half): the MINIMUM house tranche amount this cash-back is conditional on (e.g. 600000 — the same $600k a $1,200 cash-back program prices). The 3-tranche sweep may set the house mortgage BELOW its tranche's declared min_amount, forgoing this incentive; the origination inflow is credited only for a swept house amount >= this threshold. ABSENT = credited at origination unconditionally (the pre-#1075 behaviour, byte-identical — DP#13: absence is not an opinion).

cash_back.description: Issue #1075: a lender cash-back incentive on a kind=mortgage liability. Modelled as an UPFRONT cash inflow at origination plus a CONTINGENT clawback charge if the mortgage is fully prepaid before the retention term elapses. Kept as a small, documented contingent item — the schema records the terms so the clawback can be priced later, while the engine's only present effect is the origination inflow (the year-0 mortgage amortizes on a fixed schedule the engine cannot early-break, so the clawback event cannot arise yet; pricing it is the optimizer half of #1075). The inflow may be CONDITIONAL on the house tranche amount (min_house_amount) — the sweep's question is whether FORGOING the incentive by putting the house mortgage below the threshold improves the outcome.

owner.description: The borrower(s). Interest deductibility and the reduction of terminal estate are THIS person's — for a joint liability, split per the declared percentages (#601).

balance.description: The DRAWN amount. Always distinct from `limit` — the whole fix for #577 (undrawn HELOC room booked as debt).

limit.description: Required only for revolving kinds (heloc, line_of_credit); forbidden otherwise (see allOf below).

x-uncertainty.resolved_by: Your mortgage/HELOC statement, or the lender's current renewal offer.
x-uncertainty.question: What interest rate does this debt actually carry?

amortization.description: Required only for closed-end kinds (mortgage, car_loan, student_loan, personal_loan, intergenerational_loan).

collateral.description: The property this debt is registered against, or null for genuinely unsecured debt (#689). This is the ONE axis that decides whether a revolving facility counts against that property's OSFI B-20 charge limit (#664/#681) and whether it survives a sale of the property -- not the liability `kind`.

readvanceable.description: Required only for kind=heloc: whether the credit limit re-grows automatically as the paired mortgage's principal is paid down (the product mechanic the Smith Manoeuvre needs — DP#7: model the mechanism, not the branded product).

capitalize_interest.description: Required only for kind=heloc: whether unpaid interest is added to the balance rather than paid in cash.

deductible.description: Issue #1075: optional, permitted only on kind=mortgage. Whether THIS tranche's interest is deductible under ITA s.20(1)(c) — the funds were borrowed for an income-producing non-registered investment, not for the house. Absent means false (non-deductible, DP#32: absence is not an opinion, and a plain home mortgage is the ordinary case). The adapter sums the balances of every deductible tranche into property.deductible_mortgage_balance, and their exact annual interest (each balance × its own rate) into property.deductible_mortgage_interest — the true s.20(1)(c) interest base for the #850 pricing, which must NOT be derived from the blended mortgage_rate (that equals the own-rate sum only when every tranche shares one rate); the pricing itself is the optimizer half of #1075.

cash_back.description: Issue #1075: optional, permitted only on kind=mortgage. A lender cash-back incentive paid at origination (e.g. $1,200 for a $600k+ house tranche) and clawed back pro-rata if the mortgage is fully prepaid before term_years elapse. The adapter credits the declared amount as an origination_cash_back cash-flow in the projection's first year (positive to the household, non-taxable — a lender rebate, not income); the clawback-on-early-full-prepayment pricing is the optimizer half of #1075 (the year-0 mortgage here amortizes on a fixed schedule the engine cannot early-break).

open.description: Issue #651: whether the mortgage TERM is open — repayable or refinanceable at any time with NO prepayment penalty. Optional and permitted only on kind=mortgage; absent means CLOSED (the default), which triggers a break penalty of max(3 months' interest, IRD) on an early break (countries/canada/ird_penalty.compute_breakage_penalty). Openness is ORTHOGONAL to rate_type: a term can be open-fixed, open-variable, closed-fixed or closed-variable, so this is a separate axis from fixed/variable and NOT derivable from it. When true, the break penalty is a DECLARED zero (DP#32) — not the accidental zero of an unpriced or mis-typed term. A revolving line (heloc/line_of_credit) has no term to break, so `open` is forbidden there (see allOf below).

to.description: null = designation still in effect as of the document's as_of (not yet closed out).

cca.description: Optional (#694): the household's election to claim Capital Cost Allowance (depreciation) against this rental's income. Omitted/null = no CCA claimed (byte-identical to #693). Its presence commits the deferred recapture on disposition (ITA s.13(1)): CCA lowers taxable rental income now, and the previously-claimed CCA is clawed back as ordinary income at death's deemed disposition.

short_term.description: Optional (#697): non-null marks this as a SHORT-TERM rental (Airbnb-style), a legally and fiscally different animal from a long-term rental. Its income is ACTIVE business income (ITA s.9) not passive property income (T776); gross above the $30k small-supplier threshold (ETA s.148) triggers GST/HST/QST registration; and it is subject to a jurisdictional legality gate (countries/canada/short_term_rental.py) that REFUSES to model income where the tool cannot confirm the use is permitted. Omitted/null = a long-term rental (byte-identical to #693).

short_term_facts.description: The jurisdiction/registration facts a short-term rental MUST declare so the engine can rule on its legality (#697). Both required — the tool refuses to model STR income without them (DP#32: no silent 'assume legal').

jurisdiction.description: The municipality/borough this STR operates in (e.g. 'montreal_plateau_mont_royal', 'montreal_lachine'). Matched against countries/canada/short_term_rental.STR_BANNED_JURISDICTIONS; a borough on that fully-banned list refuses income outright.

citq_registered.description: Whether a valid CITQ (Corporation de l'industrie touristique du Québec) registration is held (Loi 67). false = the tool cannot confirm the use is permitted and refuses to model STR income.

cca_election.description: A Capital Cost Allowance election on a rental building (#694). The class/rate is CONFIGURATION, not a hardcoded 4%, because the correct class (build type, acquisition date, accelerated-investment eligibility) depends on facts this tool does not collect (DP#2/DP#12).

rate.description: Declining-balance CCA rate (0.04 for Class 1 residential rental).

capital_cost.description: Original capital cost of the DEPRECIABLE building (land is not depreciable) — the recapture ceiling on disposition.

opening_ucc.description: Undepreciated capital cost at the projection start (= capital_cost if no CCA was ever claimed before; less if depreciation has already been taken).

property_purchase.description: A dated mid-horizon acquisition of this property (#696, epic #690 bite 5). Its presence means the property is BOUGHT on `date` (or in `year`, #956 bite C), not held from year 0: it contributes no equity, rent, or CCA before then, and in the purchase year the household funds the down payment (value − the mortgage originated against it, at the couple's share) plus `closing_costs` out of cash. Omitted = held from the projection's first year (byte-identical to #692). Exactly one of `date` or `year` must be given (`year` is a sweepable numeric leaf, DP#32).

date.description: The acquisition date; the property enters the balance sheet (and its mortgage originates) in this calendar year.

year.description: OPTIONAL (#956 bite C): the purchase/sale calendar YEAR as a numeric leaf, a sweepable alternative to `date`. When present it is used directly; sweep it via sensitivity.sweeps (e.g. properties.N.purchase.year: [2028, 2030, 2032]) to rank timings. Exactly one of `date` or `year` must be given.

closing_costs.description: Land-transfer tax, notary, inspection and other one-time acquisition costs — a real expense in the purchase year (not recoverable equity). The couple's share is taken.

financing.description: OPTIONAL (#967): a MORTGAGE originated against this property at the purchase year. Absent = the purchase is equity-financed (the full value leaves the portfolio as the down payment), byte-identical to #696. When present, only the DOWN PAYMENT (value − mortgage_amount, couple share) leaves the portfolio; the mortgage funds the rest, originates as a serviced secured liability in the purchase year, and its interest is deductible when the property is a rental (ITA s.20(1)(c)) and non-deductible for a recreational/personal property. Mutually exclusive with `funding_options`: `financing` is the single fixed way the purchase is funded, while `funding_options` asks the optimizer to RANK alternatives (DP#22). Declaring both is a load error -- a purchase cannot be both fixed and swept.

funding_options.description: OPTIONAL (#1011): candidate FUNDING METHODS for this purchase the optimizer ENUMERATES and RANKS by the active objective (DP#22) -- 'buy this home and let the engine choose how to fund it' rather than hand-building one contract variant per funding method. Absent = the purchase is funded the single fixed way `financing` declares (or equity-financed when `financing` is absent too), byte-identical to #967/#696. When present, `financing` MUST be omitted: a purchase is either funded one fixed way or swept across alternatives, never both. At least two options are required -- a single-option `funding_options` is not a sweep, it is a (mis-)spelled `financing` and is refused at load (DP#32). Each option is one way to fund the SAME purchase (same `date`/`year`, `closing_costs`, property); the optimizer re-optimises per option and ranks by objective, so a household reads the objective-best funding in one run.

id.description: Stable identifier for this funding candidate, tagged onto every ranked result row the optimizer produces for it (e.g. 'all_cash', 'mortgage_20'). Referenced by the report to name the objective-winner.

label.description: Human-readable label for the report's ranked table.

method.description: How this candidate funds the purchase. 'all_cash' = no originated mortgage; the full value (couple share) is drawn through the liquidation waterfall as the down payment, byte-identical to #696's equity-financed behaviour. 'mortgage' = a down payment (down_pct of value) is drawn through the waterfall AND a mortgage is originated for the rest (value * (1 - down_pct)), serviced from the purchase year to payoff, interest deductible when the property is a rental (ITA s.20(1)(c)) and non-deductible otherwise -- the deductibility follows the property's `kind`, exactly like the fixed `financing` block (#967).

down_pct.description: Required when method=mortgage: the down payment as a fraction of the property's value (0.20 = 20% down). The originated mortgage_amount is value * (1 - down_pct), at the couple's share. 1.0 = a 100% down payment (equity-financed, equivalent to all_cash but spelled as a mortgage candidate with no originated debt -- the engine treats it identically).

rate.description: Required when method=mortgage: the annual interest rate as a fraction (0.05, not 5), held to payoff (a renewal schedule is a follow-up, mirroring the fixed `financing` block).

rate_type.description: Required when method=mortgage: fixed or variable, held to payoff (mirrors the fixed `financing` block).

amortization_years.description: Required when method=mortgage: the amortization period in years, serviced to a zero balance from the purchase year (mirrors the fixed `financing` block).

property_funding_option.description: Issue #1011: ONE candidate way to fund a mid-horizon property PURCHASE, for the optimizer to sweep and rank. `all_cash` draws the full value through the waterfall (no originated mortgage); `mortgage` draws a down payment and originates a mortgage for the rest. The deductibility of the mortgage interest follows the property's `kind` (rental => deductible, ITA s.20(1)(c)), never a declared tracing -- mirroring the fixed `financing` block (#967).

property_financing.description: Issue #967: a MORTGAGE originated against a property at its mid-horizon purchase year. Unlike the year-0 liabilities (which are opening balances), this liability ORIGINATES in the purchase year: its principal is an inflow that funds the purchase (only the down payment leaves the portfolio), and it is serviced (principal + interest) from the purchase year to its payoff, joining the cash-flow identity's debt-service term. The mortgage is secured by the property (collateral = the property), and its interest is deductible under ITA s.20(1)(c) when the property earns income (kind=rental) and NON-deductible for a personal/recreational property -- the deductibility follows the property's kind, not a declared tracing, mirroring how _map_owned_properties prices rental interest today. All fields required when financing is declared: a mortgage with no amount, rate, or term is not a mortgage (DP#32 -- absence fails loudly, never defaults to a guessed term).

mortgage_amount.description: The principal originated at the purchase year (the drawn amount). The couple's share is taken, mirroring liability.balance. Must be less than or equal to the property's value (a mortgage larger than the purchase price is a different, unmodelled product).

rate.description: The annual interest rate as a fraction (0.05, not 5). A fixed-rate mortgage holds this rate to its payoff this bite (no renewal schedule -- the existing amortization_schedule renewal machinery is the principal mortgage's; a mid-horizon mortgage carries a single rate, modelled on the consumer-loan servicing which amortizes at the loan's own declared rate).

rate_type.description: fixed or variable. This bite holds the declared `rate` to payoff (a renewal schedule is a follow-up); the field is required and recorded so a future renewal path can be added without a schema change (DP#9 -- one live shape).

amortization_years.description: The amortization period in years. The mortgage is serviced to a zero balance over this term from the purchase year, mirroring how the closed-end consumer loans (apply_consumer_loans) amortize at their own declared payment/term.

property_sale.description: A dated mid-horizon voluntary SALE of this property (#956 bite B), the symmetric inverse of `property_purchase` (#696). Its presence means the property LEAVES the balance sheet in the calendar year of `date` (or `year`, #956 bite C): it contributes its normal equity up to (but not including) the sale year, then zero from the sale year onward -- in the sale year itself the net proceeds (value less the secured mortgage, `selling_costs`, and the disposition tax) replace it in the portfolio, invested by the sale-year handler. Omitted/null = the property is held to the horizon (byte-identical to #692/#696). `selling_costs` is optional: a sale with no realtor/notary/inspection costs is a legitimate null, distinct from a sale that has not been priced (DP#32). Exactly one of `date` or `year` must be given (`year` is a sweepable numeric leaf, DP#32).

date.description: The disposition date; the property leaves the balance sheet in this calendar year and its net proceeds enter the portfolio.

year.description: OPTIONAL (#956 bite C): the purchase/sale calendar YEAR as a numeric leaf, a sweepable alternative to `date`. When present it is used directly; sweep it via sensitivity.sweeps (e.g. properties.N.sale.year: [2028, 2030, 2032]) to rank timings. Exactly one of `date` or `year` must be given.

selling_costs.description: Realtor commission, notary, staging and other one-time disposition costs — a real expense that reduces the net proceeds (not recoverable equity). The couple's share is taken. Absent/null = $0 in selling costs (a real declarable value, not an unknown — DP#32).

property_carrying_costs.description: Issue #1010 (epic #956): a property's RECURRING carrying costs -- property tax, maintenance, insurance, condo/HOA fees, utilities -- the holding cost of owning the home, modelled as a per-property attribute the way `rental_facts.expenses_annual` models a rental's T776 operating expenses. Active over the OWNERSHIP WINDOW (the purchase year if bought mid-horizon, else the projection start, through the sale year if sold) and charged each year as an annual cash outflow through the solvency liquidation waterfall (simulation_rules.apply_solvency), conserving money (DP#18). For a non-rental (recreational/vacant_land) this is the WHOLE holding cost; for a rental it composes with `rental_facts.expenses_annual` (the T776 net-rent expense). Both fields OPTIONAL -- a declared `{}` is a legitimate $0 (a real zero, not an unknown -- DP#32). Absent the whole block => $0 => byte-identical to today (DP#32: zero is a value, not a fallback). The flat `annual_amount` is taken at the couple's ownership share (mirroring `purchase.closing_costs`); `fraction_of_value` is applied to the couple's share of the property's CURRENT (appreciating) gross value. NOT permitted on the principal residence: its recurring costs already live in `household_budget.annual_living_costs`, so declaring them here would be a silent dead read -- the schema forbids it loudly (the allOf gate on `$defs/property`) rather than dropping it (DP#32).

annual_amount.description: A flat annual dollar amount of recurring carrying cost (property tax + maintenance + insurance + ...). The couple's ownership share is taken. Absent/null = $0 from this component (a real zero, not an unknown -- DP#32).

fraction_of_value.description: A fraction of the property's CURRENT gross value per year (e.g. 0.015 for 1.5%/yr -- property tax is often assessed on value). Applied to the couple's share of the appreciated gross value (so it composes with `appreciation_rate`). Absent/null = $0 from this component (DP#32). A sweepable numeric leaf: range it via sensitivity.sweeps.

appreciation_rate.description: OPTIONAL (#956 bite A): the property's REAL annual appreciation rate (dimensionless, e.g. 0.03 for 3%/yr; negative allowed). Absent/null = a static value, byte-identical to #692/#696 (DP#32). Its gross value compounds from the ownership year (the purchase year if dated, else the projection start), and equity = appreciated value - the secured mortgage (held static this bite; amortization is a follow-up). A sweepable numeric leaf: range it via sensitivity.sweeps (e.g. properties.N.appreciation_rate: [0, 0.03, 0.05]) so a purchase-timing conclusion is robust to the assumption rather than hostage to one guess.

designated_principal_residence_years.description: A principal-residence exemption is typically claimed per property per year, by family unit; a family with >1 property allocates which years apply to which property here (#601).

rental.description: Non-null only for kind=rental. Its presence is what auto-includes cash-damming (DP#16), replacing rental_properties.properties[] and the top-level rental_income trigger.

purchase.description: Optional (#696): a dated mid-horizon purchase. Omitted/null = the property is held from the projection's first year (byte-identical to #692).

sale.description: OPTIONAL (#956 bite B): a dated mid-horizon voluntary SALE. Omitted/null = the property is held to the horizon (byte-identical to #692/#696). When present, the property leaves the balance sheet in the sale year (equity gates to zero from that year on, see `_property_equity_for_year`) and its net proceeds (value less mortgage, selling costs, and disposition tax) are invested — see the sale-year handler.

carrying_costs.description: OPTIONAL (#1010): the property's RECURRING carrying costs (property tax, maintenance, insurance) charged each year over the ownership window through the solvency waterfall. Omitted/null = $0 => byte-identical to today (DP#32). Forbidden on the principal residence (its costs live in household_budget.annual_living_costs; declaring them here would be a silent dead read).

allOf.description: Issue #1010: carrying_costs is forbidden on the principal residence -- its recurring costs are already household_budget.annual_living_costs, so a declaration here would be a silent dead read. The schema forces it to null (absent), refusing a real value loudly (DP#32), never dropping it.

owner.description: null = household-level (not attributable to one person).

date.description: Replaces the old `.year` integer (#594) — a date, per DP#1.

annual_living_costs.description: Issue #679: the household's own measured annual working-phase spend outside any account or debt payment (housing/utilities/food/transport/etc. -- NOT the mortgage payment, which is already on liabilities[kind=mortgage], and NOT the retirement assumptions.retirement.spending_target, which only applies post-retirement). null = not measured; the cash-flow solvency invariant does not run without it (DP#16). A household that declares this omits the input entirely rather than writing 0 -- no real household spends nothing to live.

x-uncertainty.resolved_by: Your own budget: 12 months of bank/credit statements — total spend, minus debt payments and minus savings/investment contributions.
x-uncertainty.question: What does this household actually spend per year to live, outside its mortgage payment and its own savings?

discretionary_fraction.description: Issue #761: the fraction (0..1) of annual_living_costs that is DISCRETIONARY -- restaurants, alcohol, vacations, entertainment: spending a household cuts FIRST under an income shock. The remainder (1 - fraction) is NON-DISCRETIONARY (groceries, utilities, insurance, phones, transport, medicine) and stays rigid, alongside debt service and any committed installment (#759). Optional and deliberately NOT required (DP#16): omitting it reproduces today's behaviour exactly -- the solvency/runway identity treats the WHOLE scalar as rigid, and the output says so explicitly (the runway_treats_all_spend_as_rigid approximation fires), never inventing a fraction (DP#32). Under a dated income shock (decisions.income[] with an override that reduces income below baseline), the runway/solvency identity compresses the discretionary portion to ZERO -- a labelled, documented stress assumption (a household in genuine distress stops dining out and taking vacations; it does not stop buying groceries or paying insurance). 0.0 = all rigid (explicit); 1.0 = all discretionary (explicit); both are real declarable values, distinct from omitting the field.

expense_segments.description: Issue #760: dated, finite-term living-cost segments ON TOP OF the perpetual annual_living_costs scalar -- a private-school tuition that ENDS when a child ages out, childcare that ages out, a term expense that stops on a date. The scalar can only smear such a cost across the whole horizon (carrying a child's tuition through retirement and into the estate -- wrong, and wrong in the direction that makes the household look poorer than it is). Each segment is an ANNUAL recurring amount active over [from, to): it contributes its amount prorated by the days of that window falling in each calendar year (day-count blend, the outflow-side analog of #674's dated income windows), and a non-null `to` means the expense STOPS after that date (reverts to $0, never carried to the horizon). Optional and deliberately NOT required (DP#16): omitting it reproduces today's behaviour exactly (the golden invariant does not move, DP#32). Each segment folds into the solvency identity's spending outflow (simulation_rules.apply_solvency) beside annual_living_costs; a discretionary segment (non_discretionary=false) compresses to zero under an income shock exactly as #761's scalar split does, a non-discretionary one stays rigid. Requires annual_living_costs to be declared -- a dated segment WITHOUT the measured base fails loudly at the contract boundary (DP#32), never defaulting the base to zero.

emergency_reserve.$comment: Issue #688. The single most important risk decision a leveraged household makes -- 'how much do I keep OUT of the market, where, and is it enough?' -- and the contract could not express any part of it. This block is a POLICY (how many months to hold, and where), which is why it lives under assumptions rather than beside the measured household_budget.annual_living_costs it is sized against. Absent = the household holds NO reserve: a hard zero that the ruin report states explicitly, never a silent default (DP#32).

target_months.description: Months of ESSENTIAL outflows (household_budget.annual_living_costs + this year's debt service) to hold liquid. 0 is a real, declarable answer ('I hold no reserve'), distinct from omitting the block entirely -- both yield a $0 reserve, but the first is a decision and the second is an absence, and the output says which (DP#32). Sweepable: sensitivity.sweeps.emergency_reserve_months lets the optimizer show the real trade -- expected terminal wealth against the probability and cost of a forced sale.

x-uncertainty.resolved_by: A choice, not a fact. Narrow it by asking how long you would need to find comparable work, and how far your investments could fall while you looked.
x-uncertainty.question: How many months of essential outflows should be held liquid, out of the market?

held_in.description: WHERE the reserve is held -- and this is most of the answer, not a detail. A reserve held as CASH INSIDE A TFSA grows tax-free, withdraws with no tax and no penalty, and its contribution room is restored the following January, so it costs nothing in room. The same dollars in a non-registered account are taxed on their yield; in an RRSP they are effectively unavailable (a withdrawal is fully taxable and the room is gone forever). The reserve is a CASH SLEEVE CARVED OUT of the named account's declared balance -- it is not extra money on top of it, so the account's remaining balance is what stays invested at the portfolio return. null = the reserve is held outside every declared account (an ordinary chequing/savings balance the contract does not otherwise model).

instrument.description: What the reserve is held AS. A reserve modelled as compounding at the portfolio's equity return is not a reserve -- the engine grows this balance at `rate` below, never at assumptions.return_model's rate (simulation_rules.apply_emergency_reserve_growth).

rate.description: The annual return the reserve's declared `instrument` actually earns (a HISA/GIC/T-bill rate). Required rather than inferred from `instrument`: hardcoding 'cash means 2%' inside the engine would be exactly the opinion-in-code DP#2 forbids, and a household can look this rate up on its own account statement.

x-uncertainty.resolved_by: The rate your cash/HISA actually pays — read it off the account statement.
x-uncertainty.question: What rate does the cash holding the emergency reserve actually earn?

replenish_priority.description: Where refilling a drawn-down reserve ranks against other uses of surplus cash. Declared now because the reserve is meaningless without it; NOT yet consumed by the engine (the replenishment rule is follow-up work, and this field is listed in tests/test_schema_coverage.py's DEAD_ALLOWLIST as parsed-but-not-yet-read rather than quietly pretended to work).

equity_grant.$comment: Issue #768. A private-company stock-option / equity grant the household holds. This is a RECORD, not an asset: the engine values it at $0 for every solvency / runway / decumulation metric and never counts it as a liquid resource, because a private, unvested, or strike-undetermined option cannot be sold and realises only on a speculative liquidity event outside the projection. `strike` is nullable: null means 'not yet set / TBD' -- the option has no determinable value today, and the engine must say so (output 'strike TBD') rather than invent one (DP#32). `liquidity` is 'private' for a grant on a company with no public market (the case this block exists for) or 'public' for one with a listed market (still recorded, still $0 here until a dated liquidity event is modelled -- a separate, speculative input not in this block).

owner.description: The person who holds the grant (the optionee).

grantor.description: The company granting the options (the issuer). A FACT, free text -- a branded company name is fine here because it is the user's own document, not library code (DP#7 is about engine modelling, not about what a user writes in their input).

grant_date.description: The date the grant was made (the board/compensation-committee grant date).

vesting.description: The vesting schedule: a cliff date (0% vests before it -- termination before the cliff forfeits everything) and the date 100% vests.

strike.description: The per-share exercise/strike price. null = not yet set (TBD): the option has no determinable value today and the engine surfaces 'strike TBD' (DP#32: never invent a value).

liquidity.description: private = the grant is on a company with no public market (cannot be sold); public = a listed market exists. Both are recorded at $0 here until an explicitly-modelled, dated liquidity event (a separate, speculative input) -- this block is record-only.

shares.description: The number of options/shares in the grant. Optional -- a record of the size, not used to value the grant (no market price to multiply by).

fully_diluted_pct.description: The grant's share of the company on a fully-diluted basis. Optional record; not used to value the grant.

notes.description: Free-text notes (e.g. 'exercisable for 7 years after vesting', 'subject to acceleration on change of control'). A FACT about the grant's terms.

equity_vesting.$comment: Issue #768. The vesting schedule of an equity grant. `cliff_date` is the first date ANY shares vest (termination before it forfeits the entire grant -- 0% vests); `fully_vested_date` is the date 100% vests. The interim schedule (monthly/quarterly instalments between the cliff and full vesting) is free-text `schedule` -- it does not change the $0-for-solvency valuation (the grant is $0 regardless of vesting state until a dated liquidity event), so it is a record, not a rule input.

cliff_date.description: The first date any shares vest. Termination before this date forfeits the entire grant (0% vested).

fully_vested_date.description: The date 100% of the grant is vested.

schedule.description: Free-text description of the interim vesting (e.g. '25% at the 1-year cliff, then 1/36 monthly thereafter'). A record; the engine does not value partial vesting (the grant stays $0 until a dated liquidity event).

expense_segment.$comment: Issue #760. A dated, finite-term living-cost segment layered ON TOP of the perpetual household_budget.annual_living_costs scalar -- a private-school tuition that ends when a child ages out, childcare, a term expense that stops. `amount` is an ANNUAL recurring figure; the segment is active over the half-open window [from, to) and contributes `amount` prorated by the days of that window falling in each calendar year (day-count blend, the outflow-side analog of #674's dated income segments). `to` is REQUIRED and nullable: null is the EXPLICIT spelling of 'perpetual / no known end' (DP#32 -- an open-ended segment must SAY null, not omit the key), a non-null date means the expense ENDS there and contributes $0 afterwards (never carried to the horizon the way the base scalar is). `non_discretionary` is REQUIRED: true = a committed, must-pay dated expense that stays rigid under an income shock (tuition, childcare); false = a dated discretionary expense that compresses to $0 under a dated income shock exactly as #761's scalar discretionary split does. The two values are genuinely distinct decisions, so neither may be defaulted (DP#32 two-way trap). A segment can only be declared alongside a measured annual_living_costs -- the base engages the solvency module (DP#16); a segment without it is refused at load.

description.description: What the segment pays for (e.g. 'private-school tuition, child_a', 'daycare'). A FACT, free text.

amount.description: The ANNUAL recurring amount while the segment is active (same annual convention as annual_living_costs). Prorated by the days of [from, to) that fall in each calendar year, so a segment starting mid-year contributes a partial first year.

from.description: The date the segment starts (inclusive). May be before the document's as_of -- a living cost already underway at the snapshot (e.g. tuition begun last year) simply applies from the start of the projection; unlike an installment plan (#759) there is no already-paid lump to re-price, so a past `from` is honest, not refused.

to.description: The date the segment ENDS (exclusive), or null for perpetual. Required and nullable: null is the explicit DP#32 spelling of 'no known end' (an open-ended segment must declare null, never omit the key); a non-null date means the expense stops -- it contributes $0 from that date on, never carried to the horizon the way annual_living_costs is. Must be strictly after `from` (a zero/negative window is refused at load, not silently treated as $0).

non_discretionary.description: true = a committed, must-pay dated expense that does NOT compress under an income shock (tuition, childcare, insurance); false = a dated DISCRETIONARY expense that compresses to $0 under a dated income shock, exactly as #761's scalar discretionary split does. Both values are genuine, distinct decisions -- neither is defaulted (DP#32 two-way trap: silently treating a discretionary segment as rigid, or vice versa, is the exact defect the flag prevents).

active_months.$comment: Issue #882. OPTIONAL intra-year seasonality. Absent = the segment is active every day of its [from, to) window (the #760 day-count blend, unchanged). Present = a subset of calendar-month numbers (1=January .. 12=December) the segment recurs in: the ANNUAL `amount` is spent in EQUAL shares across only these months, so a bill that runs a few months a year (heating Nov-Mar -> [1,2,3,11,12]) or a one-shot charge dated to one month (property tax each July -> [7]) is resolved at MONTHLY granularity. The within-year charge counts only the active months the [from, to) window touches (a boundary month the window enters/leaves mid-way prorates by its days), and the emergency reserve is sized on the PEAK active month rather than the annual average -- a concentrated seasonal bill demands a larger reserve. An empty list or a duplicated month is refused at load (DP#32): an empty within-year window is not silently 'every month' or $0, and a repeated month is not silently de-duplicated.
active_months.description: Optional calendar months (1-12) the segment's annual amount is spent in; absent = active year-round (#760 behaviour).

installment_plan.$comment: Issue #759. A fixed-term, zero-interest installment obligation -- the contract for a medical/dental/education payment plan that is neither a liability (no drawable facility, no collateral, no prepayment/refinance) nor a perpetual living cost. `start_date` is the date of the FIRST monthly payment and MUST be on or after the document's `as_of` (the up-front lump is already paid before the snapshot; the simulation models only the remaining N payments forward from `as_of`). The final payment date -- the end of the plan's finite term -- is DERIVED as `start_date + (number_of_payments - 1) months`; it is not declared separately, so the term cannot be stated two conflicting ways (DP#32: one spelling of the fact). `rate` is REQUIRED and must be 0: a 0%-interest plan is the whole point of this block, and a stated-rate plan's interest pricing/attribution is out of scope (#759) -- a non-zero `rate` is REFUSED at load rather than silently coerced to 0 or silently honoured. `non_discretionary` is REQUIRED and must be true: an installment plan is by construction a must-pay contractual outflow that does NOT compress under an income shock (contrast #761); a `false` value is refused loudly rather than silently treated as compressible. `final_payment` is the one optional field: omitted = no balloon (a structural absence, not a silent zero -- a $0 balloon is meaningless).

owner.description: The person(s) legally bound to the payment plan.

description.description: What the plan pays for (e.g. 'orthodontic payment plan', 'tuition installment plan'). A FACT, free text.

start_date.description: The date of the FIRST monthly payment. Must be on or after the document's as_of (the up-front lump is already paid; the simulation models only the remaining installments forward).

monthly_amount.description: Each of the N equal monthly payments.

number_of_payments.description: The count of equal monthly payments. The final payment date is start_date + (number_of_payments - 1) months.

final_payment.description: Optional balloon payment made on the same date as the last monthly payment (start_date + number_of_payments - 1 months). Omitted = no balloon.

rate.description: The annual interest rate as a fraction. REQUIRED and must be 0: this block models a 0%-interest plan; a stated-rate plan's interest pricing is out of scope (#759) and a non-zero value is refused at load (DP#32).

non_discretionary.description: Required and must be true: an installment plan is a must-pay contractual outflow that does not compress under an income shock (contrast #761's discretionary split). A false value is refused at load rather than silently treated as compressible (DP#32).

rollover_override.$comment: x-uncertainty on .spousal_rollover below: same domain question as estate.default_spousal_rollover, asked per-account (#671).

x-uncertainty.resolved_by: Read the will and this account's beneficiary designation.
x-uncertainty.question: Is a spousal rollover elected on this specific account?

default_spousal_rollover.description: The spousal-rollover election in force by default for every account with a spousal beneficiary/successor_holder (in Canada: ITA s.146(8.1)/s.70(6)). Not rolling over is sometimes optimal (uses the first spouse's low brackets) — this is a FACT about what the current will/beneficiary designations say, not a decision; the sweep across rollover-vs-not lives in decisions.estate_elections. THIS IS THE FIELD THAT MAKES 'not rolling over' EXPRESSIBLE — #600's headline six-figure silent assumption.

x-uncertainty.resolved_by: Read the will and the plan beneficiary designations. In Quebec this designation can only live there.
x-uncertainty.question: Is a spousal rollover elected on the registered plans?

x-uncertainty.resolved_by: A belief about the future, not a fact anyone can look up. Bound it by your actual asset mix and re-run; this is usually the single largest driver of the answer.
x-uncertainty.question: What long-run nominal investment return should the projection assume?

return_model.description: The single source of truth for the investment return (#595A). No parallel `assumptions.investment_return` scalar exists anywhere in this schema — deleted, not documented (DP#9).

x-uncertainty.resolved_by: No document fixes a rate decades out -- only your CURRENT signed rate is a fact (see liability.rate). Narrow this by your lender's renewal offer or a published rate sheet for the term you're about to take; the years beyond that term remain a belief.
x-uncertainty.question: What rate will this borrowing actually carry over the horizon?

x-uncertainty.resolved_by: A belief, not a lookup. Bound it from a published mortality table for your age/sex cohort; the estate calculation is highly sensitive to it.
x-uncertainty.question: How long does this person live?

mortality_belief.description: Applies only to a person whose `death_date` fact is null (still living). Exactly one of assumed_death_age / assumed_death_date should be set — the loader (#582) rejects both-set or both-null.

capital_gains_inclusion.description: null = use the current-year legislated rate from the jurisdiction's code table. Non-null overrides it FOR SENSITIVITY TESTING ONLY. Bracket tables themselves are DELETED outright, not represented here at all — the code tables always win (#595H) and were never used for tax math even when present.

frozen_brackets.description: True freezes start_year's brackets across the whole horizon (DP#5 sensitivity isolation).

contribution_limit_overrides.description: null-valued sensitivity overrides for jurisdiction-specific statutory contribution limits (e.g. Canada's RRSP/TFSA room). Empty here; the Canada overlay adds rrsp_annual_max/tfsa_annual_room properties. The normal case is the whole object empty -- year-versioned statutory limits from the code table.

drawdown_tax_mode.description: Default 'net' per #579 — 'gross' exists only for back-testing the deprecated over-drawing path, not as a recommended setting.

drawdown_order.description: $defs/account_kind is the Canada overlay's closed enum of registered-account kinds; a jurisdiction-agnostic reader sees an array of strings.

liquidate_to_target.description: OPTIONAL (issue #1009): opt-in die-with-(near)-zero drawdown mode. When true the discretionary drawdown liquidates EVERY drawable FINANCIAL account the configured drawdown_order did not already exhaust (a residual sweep appended after the configured tokens — both spouses' TFSA/RRSP, the household non-reg, the slot-0 FHSA/LIF), so first_shortfall_year means 'financial savings genuinely exhausted' rather than 'the usual accounts emptied while a LIF/FHSA sits and compounds'. The LIF statutory maximum is respected on the new path. The principal residence is NOT drawn (it stays on the balance sheet / passes to the estate); the non-primary spouse's slot-1 LIRA/LIF/FHSA are not yet modelled (#901 follow-up). Absent/false = the configured order runs unchanged, byte-identical (DP#32).

account_kind.description: Jurisdiction-agnostic placeholder — a non-empty string. The Canada overlay replaces this with the closed enum shared by account.kind and retirement drawdown ordering.

x-uncertainty.resolved_by: A belief, not a lookup: nobody can measure it. Bound it from the central bank's target band and re-run.
x-uncertainty.question: What long-run inflation rate should the projection assume?

salary_growth.description: Global default; #598 leaves no room today for per-income overrides — noted as a Phase 2 addition, not blocking (see migration-plan.md).

x-uncertainty.resolved_by: A belief about decades of your own career, not a fact anyone can look up. Narrow it from your employment agreement and historical raises, but no document fixes real wage growth 20+ years out.
x-uncertainty.question: How fast does employment income grow, in real terms, over the horizon?

savings_rate.description: Target fraction of gross family income saved annually. A stated intention (belief-adjacent), swept via sensitivity.sweeps.savings_rate.

x-uncertainty.resolved_by: A stated intention for the FUTURE, not a fact -- narrow it with 12 months of your own bank/credit statements (income minus spending), which tells you what you saved, not what you will.
x-uncertainty.question: What fraction of gross family income actually gets saved each year?

default_non_reg_yield.description: Flat fallback yield belief used ONLY when a non-registered account has no holdings/product composition declared. null = composition is required (the account's holdings[] must be non-empty); non-null is a deliberately coarse fallback, not the recommended path (DP#27 prefers per-holding composition).

rate_paths.description: One canonical HELOC-rate spelling, replacing the four in #595B (heloc.rate / assumptions.heloc_rate / property.mortgage_rate / property.heloc_rate).

products.description: Synthetic product composition registry (issue #547). DP#15: synthetic names only, never real tickers.

emergency_reserve.description: Issue #688: how much the household keeps OUT of the market, WHERE, and held as WHAT. Optional (DP#16 trigger data) and deliberately NOT in this object's `required` list -- but its absence is not a neutral default: it means the household holds a $0 reserve, and the ruin report (#679) says so explicitly rather than assuming one into existence (DP#32).

horizon.description: Replaces horizon_age/projection_years (#597, #598): explicitly names WHOSE age bounds the projection instead of an implicit 'the primary'. projection_years is never authored — always derived.

contribution_allocation.description: Jurisdiction-agnostic base: only the non-registered bucket is universal. The Canada overlay adds rrsp_pct/spousal_rrsp_pct/tfsa_pct/fhsa_pct/resp_pct.

deduct_later_bracket_target.description: Income threshold below which a deferrable deduction is withheld. null when deduct_later=false. Single surviving spelling — collapses assumptions.deduct_later_bracket_target and accounts.deduct_later_bracket_target (#595C) into the one decision it actually parametrizes.

kind.description: Issue #674 (Gap 2): no default. A job-loss scenario that hands 'kind' by omission (assumed employment) is exactly the bug this field exists to prevent — an EI-shaped override would silently overstate next year's RRSP room (ITA s.146(1)). Required, so a scenario that doesn't declare it fails to load rather than being guessed.

amount.description: Annual gross amount in effect over [from, to) — same convention as $defs/income.amount.

expenses_annual.description: Issue #980 (T2125): for kind=self_employment, the total annual professional expenses deductible against this override's gross `amount` to derive NET business income over [from, to). Same convention as $defs/income.expenses_annual: the engine taxes / charges the #978 contribution stack / accrues RRSP room on (amount - expenses_annual). Absent/null = no expenses declared (taxed on the full `amount`, DP#32 absence-safe, byte-identical to pre-#980). Read only on a self_employment override.

from.description: Issue #674 (Gap 1): the date this override's amount/kind takes effect. Before this date the base income (this income_id's own declared amount, unmodified) applies — a scenario is a window, not a whole-horizon replacement.

to.description: Issue #674 (Gap 1): null = permanent (open-ended from `from` onward) — the explicit, DP#32-compliant spelling of 'no known end', not an absent/optional key. A non-null date means the override's window closes here and the income REVERTS to this income_id's base declared amount/kind (e.g. re-employment at the pre-scenario salary) — not to zero, and not held at the override's amount forever. A scenario needing recovery at a DIFFERENT post-gap income declares a second income_override for the same income_id whose own `from` starts where this one's `to` ends.

income_override.description: A dated income shock for one income_id: [from, to) uses this override's kind/amount; outside that window the base income (declared on the person's own incomes[] entry) applies unchanged. Two or more income_overrides in one income_scenario's `overrides` may target the SAME income_id with non-overlapping windows to express a shock-then-recovery-at-a-different-income schedule (issue #674's 'small schedule of segments') — the mapping layer (input_contract.py) rejects overlapping windows for the same income_id rather than silently picking one (DP#32).

income_scenario.description: Replaces scenarios.income[].members[].role matching (#598) — overrides reference income_id, which is stable regardless of how many people/incomes exist.

amortization_years.description: Issue #655: a cash-out refinance is a NEW LOAN re-amortized over its own term -- not the incumbent mortgage's remaining amortization. Required so the engine never has to silently inherit the incumbent's schedule (DP#32).

deductible_non_reg.description: Issue #792: of THIS option's cash_out advance, the dollar amount the household declares it will route into the DEDUCTIBLE non-registered account first (ITA s.20(1)(c) interest tracing is established only when the borrowed money is deployed into income-producing non-reg at the refinance -- borrowed money put into RRSP/TFSA is non-deductible forever, s.18(11)). When present, the year-0 lump-sum waterfall fronts this amount into non-reg before filling registered room; registered is then backfilled from ongoing income. Absent means the engine keeps today's internal optimization (fill registered first, non-reg gets the remainder). A declared 0 is a real choice (route nothing to deductible non-reg), distinct from absence -- both are honoured.

advance_split.description: Issue #792: a declared split of the refinance advance between the DEDUCTIBLE non-reg account and registered accounts. Optional; absent = the engine optimizes the split internally (today's behaviour).

refinance_option.description: margin_available is deleted from this shape (#593): it is not read on this path today and 'availability' already lives on the heloc liability's `limit`.

kind.description: Issue #1075: which sub-account of the 3-tranche readvanceable structure this tranche is. 'house' = the amortizing family-home mortgage; 'investment' = the amortizing mortgage tranche borrowed to invest (its interest is deductible under ITA s.20(1)(c)); 'line' = the readvanceable revolving segment (the structure's revolving_share equivalent -- its amount is the residual of the charge, never swept independently).

min_amount.description: Issue #1075: the CASH-BACK THRESHOLD for the house tranche's amount (e.g. 600000 for a $1,200 cash-back program) -- the sweep anchors its house grid here and reports whether a winning house at/above it keeps the incentive, but it is NOT a floor anymore: the sweep may put the house mortgage BELOW it (forgoing the cash-back -- the exact trade-off issue #1075 asks the optimizer to price).
